question: What does a DNS message look like on the wire, and what are its sections?
answer_hinglish:
DNS message ek binary packet hai jiska layout RFC 1035 section 4 mein fixed hai: pehle 12-byte header, phir chaar sections -- question, answer, authority aur additional. Query aur response dono ka format SAME hai; farak sirf header ke QR bit aur sections mein kya bhara hai usme hai.

Header ke 12 bytes: 2 byte ID, 2 byte flags (QR, opcode, AA, TC, RD, RA, rcode), aur chaar 16-bit counts -- qdcount, ancount, nscount, arcount. Yeh counts batate hain ki har section mein kitni entries hain; sections ke beech koi separator ya length nahi hota, isliye parser ko har entry poori padhni padti hai tab jaake agli ka start pata chalta hai. Question entry = name + type (2) + class (2). Resource record = name + type + class + TTL (4) + rdlength (2) + rdata.

Is repo mein yeh poora model src/wire.ts ke Message interface mein hai: header, questions, answers, authority, additional. decodeMessage pehle 12 bytes se kam ho toh seedha WireError ('header needs 12 bytes') phenkta hai, phir readHeader, phir chaar counts, phir har section loop mein. Ek detail: counts attacker-controlled hain, isliye koi array count se pre-size nahi hota. encodeMessage ulta kaam karta hai aur counts sections ki length se likhta hai.
why_needed: Bina layout jaane na query bana sakte ho na reply padh sakte ho. Resolver ka har kaam -- referral, CNAME, negative answer -- inhi sections ko padhne par tika hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek courier parcel jismein upar ek label (header) hai jo batata hai andar kitne envelopes kis dabbe mein hain: 1 sawaal, 3 jawab, 2 'yeh log jaante hain', 4 'extra info'. Dabbo ke beech koi divider nahi, gin ke nikaalna padta hai.
how_it_works: Bytes 0-1 ID, 2-3 flags, 4-11 counts. Offset 12 se question section shuru. Har name variable length ka hai (labels ya pointer), isliye position sequentially aage badhti hai. Records ka rdlength batata hai rdata kitna lamba hai, jisse parser agle record par pahunchta hai.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts: interfaces Header, Question, ResourceRecord, Message; decodeMessage aur encodeMessage. Test 'every supported record type and every header flag survive encode -> decode' sample() message (CNAME, A, AAAA, NS, SOA, MX, TXT, PTR, type 99) ko round trip karta hai.
advantages: Query aur response ka ek hi format, ek hi codec
Compact binary, UDP ke 512 bytes mein fit karne ke liye bana
Fixed header se ID/flags bina body padhe mil jaate hain
disadvantages: Sections ke beech koi length nahi, toh beech ka record skip nahi kar sakte
Counts attacker-controlled hain, unpe bharosa nahi kar sakte
common_mistakes: Counts dekh kar array pre-allocate kar dena
Sochna ki response ka format query se alag hai
Header ko 12 se kam bytes mein bhi parse karne ki koshish

Authority aur additional section mein kya farak hai?

question: How is a domain name like www.example.test encoded in a DNS packet, and what are the size limits?
answer_hinglish:
Wire par naam dots ke saath nahi jaata. Har label se pehle ek length byte aata hai, phir label ke bytes, aur aakhir mein ek zero byte jo root ko represent karta hai. www.example.test banta hai: 3 'www' 7 'example' 4 'test' 0. Root khud sirf ek zero byte hai.

Limits RFC 1035 se: ek label maximum 63 bytes (kyunki length byte ke upar ke 2 bits label type ke liye reserved hain -- 00 normal label, 11 compression pointer, 01 aur 10 reserved), aur poora naam wire par maximum 255 bytes, length bytes aur final zero byte ginke.

Is repo mein presentation form ek plain string hai bina trailing dot ke ('www.example.test', root = ""). nameToLabels string ko raw label Buffers mein todta hai aur checkLabels dono limits check karta hai (MAX_LABEL_LENGTH = 63, MAX_NAME_WIRE_LENGTH = 255). Decode side par readName har label par wireLength jodta hai aur 255 cross hote hi WireError. Test 'names over 255 bytes are rejected on decode and on encode; labels over 63 on encode' dikhata hai ki 4 x 63 + 3 = 255 wala sabse bada legal naam (63, 63, 63, 61 ke labels) round trip hota hai, aur 'the root name is written as one zero byte' root ko check karta hai.
why_needed: Name encoding hi DNS parsing ka sabse tricky hissa hai: variable length, compression, limits. Ise galat samjha toh baaki sab galat parse hoga.
real_world_analogy: Train ke dabbe: har dabbe par pehle board likha hai 'is dabbe mein 7 seat' phir seats, aur aakhri mein ek khaali engine (zero byte) jo batata hai train khatam.
how_it_works: Length byte L (0-63) -> L bytes label. 0 -> naam khatam. Top 2 bits 11 -> pointer (agle question mein). Wire length = sum(L + 1) + 1.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts: nameToLabels, checkLabels, MAX_LABEL_LENGTH, MAX_NAME_WIRE_LENGTH, readName mein wireLength counter. Writer.name label by label u8(length) + bytes likhta hai aur end mein u8(0).
advantages: Length-prefixed labels ko escape ki zaroorat nahi, label mein koi bhi byte ho sakta hai
Limits se parse ka kaam bounded rehta hai
disadvantages: Text form aur wire form alag hain, conversion mein bugs aate hain
255 byte limit characters mein nahi, wire bytes mein hai -- log confuse hote hain
common_mistakes: 255 ko text length (dots ke saath) samajhna
Root ko '.' string ki tarah wire par likhna
Trailing dot ko ek khaali label maan lena

question: What do the header flags QR, opcode, AA, TC, RD, RA and rcode mean, and where do they sit in the bytes?
answer_hinglish:
Header ke byte 2 aur 3 flags hain. Byte 2: QR (0x80) -- 0 query, 1 response; opcode (4 bits, (b2 >> 3) & 0x0f) -- 0 matlab standard QUERY; AA (0x04) -- jawab authoritative server se hai; TC (0x02) -- reply truncate hua, TCP par dobara poochho; RD (0x01) -- client keh raha hai 'recursion karke do'. Byte 3: RA (0x80) -- server batata hai recursion available hai; neeche ke 4 bits rcode -- NOERROR 0, FORMERR 1, SERVFAIL 2, NXDOMAIN 3, NOTIMP 4, REFUSED 5.

Yeh flags resolver ka behaviour decide karte hain. Hamara resolver upstream ko RD=0 bhejta hai (iterative), stub server client ko RA=1 deta hai, TC=1 aaya toh TCP fallback, rcode NXDOMAIN toh negative answer.

Is repo mein readHeader bitmasks se Header object banata hai aur encodeMessage wahi bits wapas pack karta hai. Byte 3 ke beech ke 3 bits (Z/AD/CD) ignore hote hain -- DNSSEC implement nahi hai. Test 'header flags are on the right bits' har flag ko akela true karke check karta hai ki sahi byte mein sahi bit set hua: qr 0x80 byte 2, aa 0x04, tc 0x02, rd 0x01, ra 0x80 byte 3, aur opcode 5 -> buf[2] = 5 << 3, NXDOMAIN -> buf[3] = 3.
why_needed: Ek bit galat jagah par ho toh real server humein response ki jagah query samjhega ya TC miss ho jayega. Flags hi protocol ki state machine hain.
real_world_analogy: Envelope par lage stamps: 'jawab hai' (QR), 'seedha malik se' (AA), 'adhoora hai, poora courier se mangao' (TC), 'aap khud dhoondh ke do' (RD), 'haan hum dhoondh dete hain' (RA), aur result code.
how_it_works: Decode: masks aur shifts byte 2/3 par. Encode: (qr?0x80:0) | ((opcode & 0x0f) << 3) | (aa?0x04:0) | (tc?0x02:0) | (rd?0x01:0), aur (ra?0x80:0) | (rcode & 0x0f).
in_this_project: src/wire.ts readHeader aur encodeMessage; RCODE aur OPCODE_QUERY constants; rcodeName debugging ke liye. decodeHeader sirf header padhta hai taaki server FORMERR mein ID wapas de sake.

Ek test har bit ki position pin karta hai
disadvantages: Z/AD/CD bits drop ho jaate hain (DNSSEC nahi)
Extended rcode (EDNS) support nahi
common_mistakes: opcode ko 4 bits ke bajaye 3 ya 5 bit shift se padhna
RA ko byte 2 mein dhoondhna
RD=1 upstream bhejna jab khud iterative resolver ho

question: What is DNS name compression and how does a compression pointer work?
answer_hinglish:
Compression ek trick hai jisse ek hi suffix packet mein baar baar na likhna pade. Agar 'example.test' offset 12 par pehle likha ja chuka hai, toh agli baar wahi naam (ya 'www.example.test' ka suffix) likhne ke bajaye 2 bytes ka pointer likhte hain: top 2 bits 11, baaki 14 bits offset. Bytes 0xC0 0x0C ka matlab 'offset 12 se naam padho'. Naam labels ki sequence ho sakti hai jo pointer par khatam ho, ya sirf pointer.

Kyun: 512-byte UDP limit mein ek response mein question, CNAME, NS, SOA sab ek hi zone ke naam repeat karte hain. Compression ke bina packet kaafi bada hota aur TCP fallback jaldi lagta.

Decode mein ek subtle baat: pointer follow karne ke baad bhi 'naam yahan khatam hua' wala end offset IN PLACE hota hai -- pointer ke 2 bytes ke baad, chahe pointed naam kitna bhi lamba ho. readName isliye pehle jump par end = pos + 2 set karta hai.

Is repo mein test 'decodes the RFC 1035 4.1.4 example' RFC ka exact example banata hai: offset 20 par F.ISI.ARPA, 40 par FOO + pointer to 20, 64 par pointer to 26 (ARPA), 92 par root, aur check karta hai name aur end dono (jaise readName(buf, 40) -> FOO.F.ISI.ARPA, end 46). Encode side par Writer.name longest already-written suffix ka pointer likhta hai.
why_needed: Packet size kam rehta hai, toh zyada responses UDP mein fit hote hain. Aur har real server compression bhejta hai, toh decoder ko support karna hi padega.
real_world_analogy: Kitaab mein 'dekhiye page 12' likh dena, poora paragraph dobara chhapne ke bajaye.
how_it_works: Length byte ke top 2 bits: 00 label, 11 pointer. Pointer target = ((b0 & 0x3f) << 8) | b1. Decoder target par jaake wahan se labels padhta rehta hai; end offset pehle pointer ke baad wala hai.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts readName (decode) aur Writer.name (encode, names map). Test 'encoding compresses repeated suffixes, case-insensitively, and is much smaller' compressed message ko compress: false wale se 100 bytes se zyada chhota expect karta hai.
advantages: Packet size kaafi kam (test mein 100+ bytes ki bachat)
Simple format: sirf 2 bytes
disadvantages: Pointers se loops aur forward references ka attack surface khulta hai
Sirf 14 bits: offset 0x4000 (16384) se aage point nahi kar sakte
common_mistakes: Pointer follow karne ke baad end offset target ke hisaab se set karna
Pointer ke baad aur labels padhne ki koshish (pointer hamesha naam ka aakhri hissa hai)
Loop protection bhool jaana

question: Which record types does the decoder understand, and what happens to a type it does not know (RFC 3597)?
answer_hinglish:
Decoder A, AAAA, NS, CNAME, PTR, MX, TXT aur SOA ko structured RData mein badalta hai; baaki har type -- OPT (41), DS, RRSIG, DNAME, SRV, sab -- { kind: "RAW", bytes } ban jaata hai, yaani rdata ke bytes jaise the waise rakhe jaate hain. Yeh RFC 3597 ka rule hai: jo type samajh nahi aata use opaque blob ki tarah handle karo, aur usme naam ho bhi toh decompress ya compress mat karo.

Kyun decompress nahi: agar hum kisi unknown type ke andar ke bytes ko naam samajh kar pointer follow karein, toh ho sakta hai woh naam ho hi nahi. Aur encode karte waqt agar unke andar ka naam compress karein, toh doosra resolver jo type nahi jaanta woh pointer resolve nahi kar payega. Isliye naye types ke andar compression RFC 3597 ne mana kiya hai.

Is repo mein RData ek TypeScript discriminated union hai (kind field). readRData type par switch karta hai; default case r.bytes(rdlength) leta hai. writeRData RAW ko w.bytes se waise hi likh deta hai. Test 'an unknown type keeps its rdata bytes as they are (RFC 3597)' type 65000 ke 'opaque' bytes round trip karta hai, aur sample() mein type 99 ka rdata [1, 2, 3, 0xc0, 0x0c] hai -- usme 0xc0 0x0c pointer jaisa dikhta hai lekin RAW hone ki wajah se kabhi follow nahi hota. formatRecord RAW ko '\# 5 010203c00c' (RFC 3597 text form) mein dikhata hai. TXT strings latin1 mein decode hoti hain taaki har byte round trip ho.
why_needed: Internet par naye types aate rehte hain. Decoder jo unknown type par crash kare ya garbage padhe, woh real responses (jaise RRSIG wale) par fail hoga.
real_world_analogy: Post office jo kisi anjaan bhasha ka letter khole bina aage bhej deta hai. Padhne ki koshish karega toh galat samjhega.
how_it_works: switch (type): A rdlength 4, AAAA 16, NS/CNAME/PTR naam, MX u16 + naam, TXT length-prefixed strings, SOA 2 naam + 5 u32; default RAW. Ant mein r.pos === rdEnd check.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts: TYPE map, RData union, readRData, writeRData, typeName (unknown ke liye 'TYPE65000'), formatRecord. PLAN.md: 'Names inside unknown rdata are never decompressed or compressed.'
advantages: Naye types se decoder kabhi nahi tootega
Discriminated union se baaki code type-safe switch kar sakta hai
RAW bytes exact round trip
disadvantages: RRSIG/DS jaise records ka koi matlab nahi nikalta (DNSSEC implement nahi hai)
DNAME bhi RAW, resolver use ignore karta hai
common_mistakes: Unknown type ke andar pointers follow karna
Unknown type ko error maan kar poora response reject karna

question: Walk through readName: how does it follow pointers, compute the end offset and enforce the limits?
answer_hinglish:
readName(buf, start) ek loop hai jo naam ke labels padhta hai aur { name, end } return karta hai. Chaar state variables: pos (abhi kahan hain), runStart (jis label run mein hain uska start), end (-1 jab tak pehla pointer nahi mila), jumps aur wireLength (shuru 1, final zero byte ke liye).

Har iteration: pehle pos >= buf.length toh 'runs past the end'. Phir length byte len aur kind = len & 0xc0. Agar 0xc0 (pointer): second byte exist karta hai check (pos + 1 >= buf.length -> 'truncated: compression pointer'), target nikalo, target >= runStart toh reject ('does not point backwards'), ++jumps > MAX_POINTER_JUMPS (32) toh reject, pehli baar ho toh end = pos + 2, phir pos = runStart = target. Agar kind 0x40 ya 0x80 -> 'reserved label type'. Agar len 0 -> naam khatam; end abhi bhi -1 ho (koi pointer nahi tha) toh end = pos + 1. Warna label: bounds check, wireLength += len + 1 aur 255 se zyada toh reject, escapeLabel se text, pos aage.

end ka logic important hai: Reader.name() caller ko end deta hai, jo pointer ke 2 bytes ke baad hai, pointed naam ke end ke baad nahi. Agar end target ke basis par set hota toh agla field (type, class) galat jagah se padha jaata. Test 'decodes the RFC 1035 4.1.4 example' har case mein end bhi assert karta hai. Do loop rules (backwards-only, max 32 jumps) aur do size rules (label bounds, 255) milke guarantee dete hain: loop hamesha khatam, kaam bounded, buffer ke bahar kabhi nahi.
why_needed: Untrusted packet ka sabse khatarnak hissa naam hai: variable length, pointers, loops. Ek function mein saare rules rakhne se audit aasaan.
real_world_analogy: Treasure hunt jismein har chit par likha hai 'agla hint peeche page X par'. Rule: hamesha peeche hi jaana, aur 32 chits se zyada nahi. Aur aapki apni jagah wahi rehti hai jahan pehli chit mili thi.
how_it_works: Loop: bounds -> kind -> pointer(bounds, backwards, jumps, end once, jump) | reserved -> error | zero -> return | label(bounds, length cap, push).
in_this_project: src/wire.ts readName; Reader.name() isko call karke pos = end karta hai. Tests: RFC 4.1.4 example, self-pointer, A -> B -> A, forward pointer, chain of 32 vs 33, half pointer, reserved label types, names over 255.
advantages: Ek function, saare rules, har error ka precise message offset ke saath
Termination proof simple: targets strictly decrease
disadvantages: Recursion nahi, lekin har label ke liye escapeLabel string banata hai -- thoda allocation
Backwards-only rule RFC se strict hai (RFC 'prior occurrence' kehta hai, toh legal packets yahi karte hain)
common_mistakes: end ko har pointer par overwrite karna
runStart update na karna (tab A -> B -> A pakda nahi jaata)
wireLength sirf in-place labels ka ginna, pointed labels ka nahi
follow_up_questions: runStart ki jagah sirf 'target < pos' check karte toh kya galat hota?
32 jumps kaafi kyun hain?
Recursive implementation mein kya risk hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Strict backwards-only rule simple proof deta hai lekin RFC se thoda zyada strict hai; real servers sirf pehle likhe naam ko point karte hain, toh interop loss practically nahi hota (live test 6/6 pass).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar end galat set ho toh baaki message misaligned padha jaayega -- yeh silent corruption hai, crash nahi; isliye test end bhi assert karta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Visited-offsets set rakhna (loop detect), sirf jump counter rakhna, ya recursion with depth limit. Visited set memory leta hai; sirf counter bina backwards rule ke bhi terminate karta hai lekin har naam 32 jumps tak ka kaam kar sakta hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Naam per kaam bounded hai (max 32 jumps, 255 bytes), toh 10x-100x packets par bhi per-packet cost linear hai packet size mein. Hot path mein escapeLabel string allocation pehla optimisation target hota (abhi measure nahi kiya).
advanced.production_improvements: Fuzz corpus ko CI mein seed ke saath badhana, coverage-guided fuzzing (jaise jazzer.js), aur decode errors ko metrics mein count karna (kaun sa server garbage bhej raha hai).

question: How does the encoder decide where to write a compression pointer (Writer.name)?
answer_hinglish:
Writer ek Map rakhta hai: canonical suffix -> offset jahan woh pehli baar likha gaya. Writer.name(name) naam ko labels mein todta hai aur i = 0 se chalta hai: har step par labels.slice(i) ka canonical key banata hai (lowercase, escaped, dot-joined). Agar yeh key map mein hai aur compress on hai, toh 0xC000 | offset ka 2-byte pointer likh ke return -- yahi LONGEST matching suffix hai kyunki hum sabse lambe suffix se shuru karte hain. Nahi hai toh is suffix ko current offset ke saath map mein daalo, label likho, aur agle chhote suffix par jao. Koi match nahi mila toh end mein zero byte.

Do details. Pehla, map mein sirf tab daalte hain jab this.len < 0x4000, kyunki pointer mein 14 bits hain -- 16384 se aage ke offset ko point hi nahi kar sakte. Doosra, key asciiLower se banta hai, toh compression case-insensitive hai: 'WWW.EXAMPLE.TEST' baad mein aaye toh 'www.example.test' ka pointer banega. DNS names case-insensitive hain toh yeh legal hai, lekin decode par repeat pehli occurrence ke case mein wapas aata hai.

Rdata ke andar ke naam (NS host, CNAME target, MX exchange, SOA mname/rname) bhi isi Writer.name se jaate hain, toh woh bhi compress hote hain; RAW bytes kabhi nahi. compress: false option writeRDataNoCompress use karta hai -- sirf tests size compare karne ke liye.
why_needed: Encoder ko compression karna chahiye taaki stub server ke responses 512 bytes ke andar rahein aur kam baar TC=1 dena pade.
real_world_analogy: Ek writer jo har likhe hue address ka index rakhta hai: 'Andheri, Mumbai' pehle page 1 par likha tha, toh ab sirf 'Flat 4, (dekho page 1)' likhta hai.
how_it_works: names: Map<string, number>. For i in 0..labels.length: key = suffix(i); hit -> u16(0xc000 | at), return; miss -> set(key, len) if len < 0x4000, write label. End -> u8(0).
in_this_project: src/wire.ts class Writer: name(), names map, grow(); encodeMessage questions aur records dono ke naam isi se likhta hai. Test 'encoding compresses repeated suffixes...' check karta hai small.includes([0xc0, 12]) -- upper-case repeat question ke offset 12 ka pointer bana.
advantages: Longest suffix match automatically, simple loop se
Har naya suffix register hota hai, toh baad ke naam pehle wale ke beech mein bhi point kar sakte hain
0x4000 guard se kabhi invalid pointer nahi
disadvantages: Har naam par O(labels^2) string building (labels chhote hain toh practically theek)
Case information repeat names mein kho jaati hai
common_mistakes: 0x4000 limit bhool jaana -- bade TCP message mein offset overflow hokar galat jagah point karta
Case-sensitive key rakhna (compression kam hoti hai, galat nahi)
Unknown type ke rdata ke andar naam compress karna

question: In readRData, why does a name inside rdata get its own check against rdlength, and why is there a final r.pos !== rdEnd check?
answer_hinglish:
rdlength record header mein likha hota hai ki rdata kitne bytes ka hai, lekin NS/CNAME/MX/SOA ke rdata mein naam hai jiski length naam khud decide karta hai (labels ya pointer). Toh do cheezein alag-alag galat ho sakti hain: naam rdlength se bahar nikal jaaye, ya naam rdlength se pehle khatam ho jaaye aur kuch bytes bach jaayein. Dono ko reject karna zaroori hai.

readRData shuru mein r.need(rdlength) se confirm karta hai ki itne bytes packet mein hain, rdEnd = rdStart + rdlength nikalta hai, aur ek chhota closure name() banata hai: naam padho, aur agar r.pos > rdEnd ho gaya toh 'name in rdata runs past rdlength'. Dhyan do: naam ka POINTER kahin bhi pehle message mein point kar sakta hai -- check sirf in-place bytes par hai. Type-specific checks bhi hain: A ke liye rdlength 4, AAAA 16, MX kam se kam 3, SOA mein dono naamon ke baad 20 bytes bache hon, TXT ki har string rdEnd ke andar.

Aakhri line if (r.pos !== rdEnd) throw '<TYPE> rdata used X of Y bytes' -- yahi W7 mutation ka gap tha. Iske bina NS rdata mein 2 junk bytes ho toh decoder unhe chhod ke nahi, BALKI next record unhi bytes se padhna shuru karta -- yaani ek record ke beech se doosra record parse. Test 'rdata with bytes left over after the name is rejected, not read as the next record (added after mutation W7)' NS ke rdata mein 0xaa 0xbb daal kar /NS rdata used/ expect karta hai.
why_needed: Mismatch wale records ya toh buggy server ka sign hain ya attacker ka trick jisse ek record ke andar doosra record chhupaya jaa sake. Strict check se parser hamesha record boundaries par synced rehta hai.
real_world_analogy: Dabbe par likha hai '10 kg', andar ka saamaan 8 kg nikla -- bache 2 kg kahan se aaye? Ya saamaan 12 kg ka -- baaki doosre ke dabbe mein ghus gaya. Dono case mein parcel reject.
how_it_works: need(rdlength) -> rdEnd -> type switch (names via guarded closure) -> r.pos === rdEnd assert. RAW ke liye bytes(rdlength) seedha exact.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts readRData aur readRecord. Tests: 'rdlength must match the record type and the bytes the rdata really uses' (A with rdlength 5, CNAME with rdlength 5 jabki naam 16 bytes ka) aur W7 wala NS junk test.
advantages: Parser hamesha record boundary par synced
Precise errors: type, used bytes, declared bytes
Pointer flexibility bachi rehti hai (target kahin bhi pehle)
disadvantages: Kuch sloppy servers jo extra padding bhejte hain, unke responses reject honge
Har type ke liye alag rule likhna padta hai
common_mistakes: Sirf 'past rdlength' check karna aur 'leftover' bhool jaana (W7)
Pointer target ko bhi rdata ke andar hona zaroori samajhna (galat, woh pehle message mein kahin bhi ho sakta hai)
rdlength par bharosa karke bina need() ke subarray lena
follow_up_questions: Leftover bytes ko silently skip karna (r.pos = rdEnd) kyun nahi chuna?
SOA ke 20 bytes ka check kis cheez ko bachata hai?
W7 ko pehle koi test kyun nahi pakad paaya?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Strict mismatch reject vs lenient skip: strict se desync aur smuggling khatam, cost yeh ki bahut kharab servers ke responses reject; resolver tab next server try karta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Bina final check ke: record ke andar chhupa doosra record parse ho sakta hai, ya counts ke hisaab se poora baaki message misaligned. Bina name guard ke: naam rdlength ke bahar se bytes kha jaata.
advanced.alternatives: Har type ke liye alag sub-Reader jiska buffer sirf rdata tak ho (rdata slice); lekin tab pointers jo pehle message mein point karte hain resolve nahi honge, isliye closure guard chuna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Har record par ek extra comparison -- cost negligible. Zyada types (SRV, CAA, SVCB) aane par har type ka check yahi pattern follow karega.
advanced.production_improvements: Naye types ke liye table-driven rdata schema, aur property test: encode(random record) -> decode -> same, plus har rdlength +-1 mutation par WireError.

question: How does encodeMessage pack the header flags and fill in rdlength when it does not know the rdata size up front?
answer_hinglish:
Header ke flags do bytes mein bitwise OR se pack hote hain: byte 2 = (qr ? 0x80 : 0) | ((opcode & 0x0f) << 3) | (aa ? 0x04 : 0) | (tc ? 0x02 : 0) | (rd ? 0x01 : 0), byte 3 = (ra ? 0x80 : 0) | (rcode & 0x0f). Masks (& 0x0f) ensure karte hain ki galat value doosre bits ko kharab na kare.

rdlength ki problem: record likhte waqt rdlength rdata se PEHLE aata hai, lekin rdata ka size likhne ke baad pata chalta hai -- khaas kar naam wale rdata mein, kyunki compression decide karti hai ki naam full jaayega ya 2-byte pointer. Solution backpatching: lenAt = w.len yaad rakho, placeholder w.u16(0) likho, rdata likho, phir rdlength = w.len - lenAt - 2 nikalo aur w.patchU16(lenAt, rdlength) se wapas jaake sahi value daal do.

encodeMessage limits bhi check karta hai: section mein 65535 se zyada entries, rdata 65535 se lamba, ya poora message 65535 bytes se bada -- sab WireError. Writer ka buffer 512 bytes se shuru hota hai aur grow() zaroorat par double karta hai, aur done() exact length ka copy return karta hai. Test 'header flags are on the right bits' bytes check karta hai, aur 'rdlength must match...' test encode kiye hue A record ka rdlength 4 aur compressed CNAME ka 16 (1 + 13 label bytes + 'test' ka pointer) verify karta hai.
why_needed: Compression ke saath rdata size pehle se calculate karna mushkil aur error-prone hota; backpatch se ek pass mein sahi encoding.
real_world_analogy: Form bharte waqt 'total pages' wala box khaali chhod do, saare pages likh lo, phir gin ke box bhar do.
how_it_works: Write placeholder -> write body -> compute length from cursor difference -> overwrite placeholder. Same trick TCP length prefix ya HTTP Content-Length ke liye bhi use hoti hai.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts encodeMessage, Writer.patchU16, Writer.grow, Writer.done.
advantages: Ek pass encoding, compression ke saath bhi sahi length
Masks se out-of-range values doosre flags nahi bigaadti
disadvantages: Writer ko random access chahiye (patch), pure stream par yeh nahi hota
Buffer double hone par copy cost
common_mistakes: rdlength pehle se naam ki string length se calculate karna
Placeholder ke 2 bytes ko length mein gin lena
opcode ko mask kiye bina shift karna
follow_up_questions: Writer buffer 512 se hi kyun shuru hota hai?
Encode side limits (65535) kahan se aati hain?

question: How are presentation escapes like \. and \DDD handled, and why can a label containing a dot never be confused with two labels?
answer_hinglish:
Wire par label length-prefixed hai, toh label mein koi bhi byte ho sakta hai -- dot (0x2e), backslash, zero, 0xff bhi. Lekin is repo mein naam ek string hai jismein dot label separator hai. Agar 'a.b' ek label ho aur hum ise seedha 'a.b' likh dein toh woh do labels lagega. Isliye presentation escapes: label ka dot '\.' banta hai, backslash '\\', aur non-printable byte (<= 0x20 ya >= 0x7f) '\DDD' (teen decimal digits, jaise '\007').

escapeLabel decode side par yahi karta hai: 0x2e ya 0x5c -> backslash + char, printable 0x21-0x7e -> as is, baaki -> '\' + padStart(3). nameToLabels ulta karta hai: backslash ke baad teen digits hon toh woh byte (255 se zyada -> WireError), warna agla character literal, string backslash par khatam ho toh error; unescaped dot label todta hai, khaali label (jaise 'a..b') error, non-ASCII character (> 0x7e) error.

Is wajah se round trip exact hai aur label boundaries kabhi shift nahi hoti. Test 'a label containing a dot or a non-printable byte is escaped, and round-trips as ONE label' 'a\.b\007c.example.test' ko teen labels mein todta hai, pehla [0x61, 0x2e, 0x62, 0x07, 0x63], aur encode -> decode ke baad wahi string wapas. Security angle: isSubdomain('a\.example.test', 'example.test') false hai, kyunki pehla label 'a.example' hai -- naam example.test ke neeche nahi hai.
why_needed: Bina escapes ke ek attacker label 'evil.example' bana sakta hai jo text mein 'evil' + 'example' ke neeche dikhe. Escapes text form ko unambiguous banate hain.
real_world_analogy: CSV file mein comma wala value quotes mein likhte hain taaki woh do columns na ban jaaye. Yahan dot ke saath wahi -- backslash quote ka kaam karta hai.
how_it_works: Decode: bytes -> escapeLabel -> text. Encode: text -> nameToLabels (escape parse) -> bytes. canonicalName bhi escaped form ko lowercase karta hai, toh 'A\.B' aur 'a\.b' same key.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts escapeLabel, nameToLabels, canonicalName, isSubdomain. Tests: escape round trip, isSubdomain whole-label test.
advantages: Har byte sequence ka unique text form
Same convention dig/zone files use karte hain, toh output familiar
Label boundaries text mein bhi safe
disadvantages: Har jagah string parsing; Buffer[] labels se thoda slow
Space (0x20) bhi \032 ban jaata hai, readability kam
common_mistakes: Naam ko split('.') se todna (escaped dot bhool jaana)
Escape parsing mein \DDD > 255 accept kar lena
Non-printable bytes ko utf8 string mein daal dena
follow_up_questions: IDN (unicode domain) yahan kaise aayega? (punycode, xn--)
Space wala label kaise dikhega?

question: How does the decoder protect against compression pointer loops, and why does it use two independent rules?
answer_hinglish:
Do rules hain, aur dono alag kaam karte hain. Rule 1 -- backwards only: pointer ka target current label run ke start (runStart) se STRICTLY pehle hona chahiye. Har jump ke baad runStart = target, toh targets strictly decrease hote hain; offsets non-negative integers hain, toh yeh sequence finite hai aur loop impossible. Pointer to itself (offset 12 par 0xc0 0x0c) aur A -> B -> A (12 par 'a' + pointer to 16, 16 par pointer to 12) dono reject. Forward pointer bhi reject, chahe woh loop na banaye -- test 'a forward pointer is rejected even when it would not loop'.

Rule 2 -- MAX_POINTER_JUMPS = 32: rule 1 termination deta hai lekin work bound nahi. Attacker ek lamba backwards chain bana sakta hai (har pointer 2 bytes peeche), aur har naam ke liye hazaaron jumps; agar packet mein bahut saare naam same chain par point karein toh CPU ka kaam quadratic-ish ho jaata. 32 ka cap per-name kaam bounded karta hai. Real names ko kuch hi pointers chahiye hote hain.

Kyun dono: rule 1 akela -> terminates but expensive; rule 2 akela -> bounded but self-loop ko bhi 32 baar ghumega aur naam ka 'meaning' undefined. PLAN.md: 'The first rule alone guarantees termination; the cap bounds the work. Both are tested separately.' Mutation checks yahi dikhate hain: W1 (forward allowed) 2 tests ne pakda, W2 (no cap) 1 test ne -- 'a backwards chain of more than 32 pointers is rejected; exactly 32 is fine'.
why_needed: Pointer loop classic parser DoS hai: ek chhota packet resolver ko infinite loop ya stack overflow mein daal sakta hai. Resolver internet se aaye untrusted packets padhta hai.
real_world_analogy: Seedhi pe sirf neeche utarne ka rule ho toh aap kabhi gol nahi ghoom sakte, ground par pahunchoge hi. Lekin 1000 seedhiyan ho sakti hain -- isliye '32 se zyada seedhi nahi' bhi.
how_it_works: Pointer branch: target >= runStart -> WireError; ++jumps > 32 -> WireError; warna pos = runStart = target.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts readName aur MAX_POINTER_JUMPS. Tests 'a pointer to itself is rejected (loop)', 'a two-pointer loop A -> B -> A is rejected', forward pointer test, chain(32) ok aur chain(33) /more than/. Fuzz test pointer bytes ko bias karta hai (har 7th byte 30% chance 0xc0 | random) taaki yeh paths hit hon.
advantages: Termination ka proof ek line ka
Work per name constant se bounded
Dono rules alag tested aur alag mutations se verified
disadvantages: Forward pointers jo technically harmless hon woh bhi reject (real servers bhejte nahi)
32 ek arbitrary constant hai
common_mistakes: Sirf jump counter rakhna aur backwards rule chhodna
runStart ki jagah start (naam ka shuru) se compare karna
Recursive decode bina depth limit ke
follow_up_questions: Visited set se loop detect karna better kyun nahi?
Agar backwards rule hai toh 32 cap ka mutation (W2) pakadne ke liye test kaisa hona chahiye?
Kya koi legitimate server forward pointer bhejta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Strict rules (no forward pointers) simplicity aur proof dete hain; ek theoretical RFC-legal edge case kho jaata hai. Cap 32 work aur legit names ke beech balance hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Bina rule 1: self-loop par infinite loop (process hang, saare clients blocked kyunki Node single-threaded hai). Bina rule 2: lambe chains se CPU amplification.
advanced.alternatives: Visited bitmap per name, global per-packet jump budget, ya decompressed names ka cache by offset (bind jaise implementations memo karte hain).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x traffic par per-packet worst case bounded hai (packet size x 32 per name), isliye attacker CPU amplify nahi kar sakta; fir bhi per-source rate limiting chahiye (implement nahi hai).
advanced.production_improvements: Per-packet total jump budget bhi jodna, decode errors ka metric/source IP log, aur coverage-guided fuzzing CI mein.

question: The header counts and lengths come from an attacker. How does the decoder avoid out-of-bounds reads and huge allocations?
answer_hinglish:
Packet ka har number -- qdcount, ancount, rdlength, label length -- attacker likh sakta hai. Teen defences hain.

Pehla, har read bounds checked hai. Reader class ke u8/u16/u32/bytes sab pehle need(n, what) call karte hain: pos + n > buf.length toh WireError 'truncated: <what> needs n byte(s) at offset X'. readName apne bounds khud check karta hai (label, pointer ka second byte, run past the end). Node ka Buffer waise bhi out of range par undefined ya RangeError deta, lekin humein HAR malformed input par sirf WireError chahiye -- fuzz test yahi assert karta hai ki 'nothing else' throw ho.

Doosra, counts se koi array pre-size nahi hota. ancount = 65535 likh do, decoder [] se shuru karke push karta hai; har question kam se kam 5 bytes aur har record kam se kam 11 bytes khaata hai, toh buf.length / 5 iterations ke andar bounds check fail ho jaata hai. Test 'a count larger than the packet is a clean error, not a huge allocation' yahi karta hai: ancount 0xffff, koi answer nahi -> /truncated/.

Teesra, bytes() COPY karta hai (Buffer.from(subarray)), taaki ek chhota RAW record poore packet ko memory mein zinda na rakhe. Aur rdata ke liye pehle r.need(rdlength) -- 60000 ka rdlength 100-byte packet mein turant reject.

Mutation W9 (Reader.need bounds check removed) 2 tests ne pakda. File ke upar comment: 'never reads past the buffer, never loops forever and never allocates more than the packet itself could describe'.
why_needed: Parser bugs (out-of-bounds read, allocation bomb) DNS software ke classic CVEs hain. Resolver internet ke kisi bhi server ka reply padhta hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank cashier form par likha 'mujhe 10 crore do' padh ke vault nahi kholta; pehle dekhta hai account mein kitna hai. Count ek claim hai, packet ki length sachchai.
how_it_works: Reader.need -> WireError. Loops count tak chalte hain lekin har iteration bytes consume karti hai, toh bounded by buffer. bytes() copy.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts Reader (need, u8, u16, u32, bytes), decodeMessage ka comment 'No array is pre-sized from a count', readRData ka r.need(rdlength). Tests: count test, truncation at every offset, 6000 fuzz packets.
advantages: Ek hi error type, caller ka handling simple
Allocation packet size se bounded
Error message mein offset aur field ka naam -- debugging easy
disadvantages: Har read par ek comparison (negligible)
bytes() copy thodi memory/CPU leta hai
common_mistakes: new Array(count) se pre-allocate
Buffer ke undefined ko 0 maan ke aage badhna
subarray rakh lena jisse poora packet GC na ho
follow_up_questions: Kya 'bytes after the last record are ignored' ek risk hai?
Fuzz test ne kya guarantee kiya aur kya nahi?
TCP par 64 KB message mein yeh bounds kaafi hain?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Strict bounds har field par thoda code badhata hai lekin parser ka trust boundary ek jagah (Reader) aa jaata hai. Copy vs view: copy memory safety (no retention) deta hai, view zero-copy.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Bina need(): Buffer readUInt16BE RangeError phenkta (WireError nahi), toh caller ka 'next server' logic toot sakta tha; ya undefined ko number samajh ke silent garbage.
advanced.alternatives: Schema-driven parsers (kaitai), Rust jaisi memory-safe language, ya WebAssembly sandbox. Node mein Buffer already memory-safe hai, toh yahan focus error type aur DoS par hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Allocation per packet O(packet size) hai, toh 100x traffic par memory linear badhti hai; burst mein GC pressure ho sakta hai -- tab view + careful lifetime ya pooling sochna padega (abhi measure nahi kiya).
advanced.production_improvements: Decode failures ka metric per upstream, max message size TCP par enforce, aur fuzzing ko coverage-guided banana.

question: Why does isSubdomain compare names label by label instead of using endsWith?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki string endsWith galat jawab deta hai. 'badexample.test'.endsWith('example.test') true hai, lekin badexample.test example.test ke NEECHE nahi hai -- woh test ke neeche ek alag zone hai. Aur escaped dot wala case: 'a\.example.test' ka pehla label 'a.example' hai (ek hi label), toh yeh bhi example.test ke neeche nahi.

Resolver ka bailiwick rule isi function par tika hai: 'server for zone Z sirf Z ya uske neeche ke records sikha sakta hai'. Agar yahan endsWith hota, toh example.test ka server badexample.test ke records inject kar paata -- cache poisoning ka darwaza.

isSubdomain dono naamon ko splitCanonical se canonical labels mein todta hai (nameToLabels + escapeLabel + asciiLower), phir peeche se label by label compare karta hai. Parent zyada labels wala ho toh false. Root ('') ke neeche sab kuch hai. Case-insensitive bhi hai: 'EXAMPLE.test' aur 'example.TEST' same.

Test 'isSubdomain compares whole labels' saare cases check karta hai: www.example.test under example.test true, khud apne under true, anything.test under '' true, badexample.test false, 'a\.example.test' false, case mix true, aur 'test' under example.test false. PLAN.md mein likha hai: 'never a plain endsWith'.
why_needed: Bailiwick aur zone cut logic ka base yahi hai; galat comparison = security bug.
real_world_analogy: Address 'Sector 15, Noida' ke neeche 'Flat 3, Sector 15, Noida' aata hai, lekin 'Sector 115, Noida' nahi, chahe string ke end mein '15, Noida' dikhe.
how_it_works: c = labels(child), p = labels(parent); p.length > c.length -> false; for i in 1..p.length: c[c.length - i] === p[p.length - i] warna false.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts isSubdomain, splitCanonical, parentName (pehla label hatata hai), labelCount. Resolver aur cache inhe use karte hain, lekin comparison logic wire.ts mein hai.
advantages: Label boundaries aur escapes respect karta hai
Case-insensitive, DNS rules ke mutabiq
Chhota, test karna aasaan
disadvantages: Har call par naam re-parse hota hai (string se labels)
common_mistakes: endsWith ya regex se check
Case-sensitive compare
Escaped dot ko separator samajhna
follow_up_questions: Bailiwick check mein isSubdomain kahan aata hai?
'.' + parent se endsWith karte toh kaunsa case abhi bhi toot-ta?

question: What happens when a packet cannot be decoded, both on the resolver side and on the stub server side?
answer_hinglish:
wire.ts ka contract simple hai: kuch bhi malformed ho toh sirf WireError throw hota hai, kabhi koi aur exception nahi, kabhi partial result nahi. Iske upar har caller apna policy lagata hai.

Resolver side (src/transport.ts): UDP par agar aaya hua packet decode nahi hota, toh use IGNORE kiya jaata hai (onIgnored('undecodable')) aur socket wait karta rehta hai -- kyunki ho sakta hai yeh attacker ka garbage ho aur asli reply abhi aane wala ho. Timeout tak kuch sahi na aaye toh TimeoutError. TCP par decode fail ho toh WireError seedha query ko fail karta hai. Resolver ka askZone WireError, TimeoutError aur TransportError teeno ko same treat karta hai: trace line likho aur zone ke next server par jao. wire.ts ke header comment mein yahi likha hai: 'The resolver treats a WireError from a server like a timeout: try the next server.'

Stub server side (src/server.ts): pehle decodeHeader -- yeh sirf 12 bytes padhta hai. 12 se kam bytes hain toh packet drop, kyunki ID hi nahi hai jawab dene ke liye. Header mil gaya lekin decodeMessage WireError de, toh FORMERR usi ID ke saath. Isi liye decodeHeader alag exported function hai. Test 'decodeHeader reads the id of a packet whose body is garbage' ek body [0xc0] (half pointer) wale packet se id 0x1234 aur rd true nikalta hai, aur 11 bytes par WireError.
why_needed: Ek single error type se callers ka failure handling consistent rehta hai. Aur 'garbage = ignore, wait' rule attacker ko cheap failures cause karne se rokta hai.
real_world_analogy: Doctor ko unreadable prescription mile toh woh dawai nahi deta, pharmacy ko wapas phone karta hai (FORMERR). Aur agar envelope par sender ka naam bhi nahi, toh phek deta hai.
how_it_works: decodeMessage -> WireError. Transport UDP: ignore + keep waiting. TCP: fail. Resolver: next server. Server: header ok -> FORMERR, header broken -> drop.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts WireError, decodeHeader, decodeMessage. Callers: transport.ts (onIgnored 'undecodable'), resolver.ts askZone (WireError -> next server), server.ts handle (FORMERR). Fuzz tests prove 'WireError and nothing else'.
advantages: Ek error type, har layer ki apni policy
Spoofed garbage se lookup fail nahi hota
Client ko FORMERR milta hai, timeout nahi
disadvantages: UDP par garbage ignore karne se ek broken server ka pata timeout ke baad hi chalta hai
Koi metric nahi ki kaun sa upstream garbage bhejta hai (sirf trace)
common_mistakes: catch (e) mein har exception ko WireError maan lena (real bugs chhup jaate hain) -- server sirf WireError catch karta hai
Header bhi na ho toh bhi reply bhejne ki koshish
Garbage reply par turant fail karna (attacker ko DoS ka sasta tareeka)
follow_up_questions: UDP aur TCP par policy alag kyun hai?
FORMERR mein question section kyun nahi bhejte?

question: What goes wrong if the decoder accepts rdata that uses fewer bytes than rdlength says (mutation W7)?
answer_hinglish:
Record parser desync ho jaata hai: decoder ek record ke rdata ke BEECH se agla record padhna shuru kar deta hai. Iske bina check ke readRData naam padh ke return kar deta, r.pos rdEnd se pehle hota, aur readRecord ka next call wahin se 'name, type, class, ttl' padhta. Bache hue bytes ab agle record ke header ki tarah interpret hote.

Yeh crash nahi hai, yeh silent corruption hai -- sabse khatarnak type ki failure. Attacker ek NS record ke rdata ke andar poora ek fake A record chhupa sakta hai: jo software rdlength respect karta hai use woh dikhega hi nahi, aur jo nahi karta use extra record milega. Do parsers ka ek hi packet ko alag padhna request smuggling jaisa hai.

Is repo mein yeh gap mutation checks se mila. W7 = 'rdata may use fewer/more bytes than rdlength' -- pehle run mein 0 tests fail hue. Kyun: koi bhi test aisa rdata nahi banata tha jisme naam ke baad bytes bache hon. Fix: naya test 'rdata with bytes left over after the name is rejected, not read as the next record (added after mutation W7)'. Woh NS record (ns.a.test) ke baad ek A record wala message encode karta hai, offset 12 + 12 + 10 par NS ka rdlength padhta hai, rdata ke end par 0xaa 0xbb insert karta hai aur rdlength 2 badha deta hai. Expect: /NS rdata used/. README: re-run par W7 exactly isi naye test se pakda gaya.
why_needed: Rdlength aur actual content mein mismatch accept karna parser differential attacks aur cache poisoning ka raasta hai.
real_world_analogy: Train ke dabbe mein 10 seats likhi hain, 8 hi nikli -- agar bache 2 ko agle dabbe ka engine maan lo, toh poori train ki ginti galat.
how_it_works: readRecord: name, type, class, ttl, rdlength, readRData. readRData ka aakhri check r.pos === rdEnd records ko aligned rakhta hai.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts readRData final check; test/wire.test.ts W7 test. README mutation table: W7 '0 (not caught) -> 1 with the new test'.
advantages: Ek line ka check, poore class of bugs khatam
Error message mein type aur used/declared bytes
disadvantages: Lenient servers ke responses reject (resolver next server try karta hai)
common_mistakes: Sirf 'past rdlength' guard rakhna, 'short' case bhool jaana
Leftover ko chupchaap skip karna bina soche ki kya chhupa tha
Yeh maan lena ki round-trip test is case ko cover karta hai (encoder kabhi aisa packet nahi banata)
follow_up_questions: Skip (r.pos = rdEnd) aur reject mein se kya chunoge aur kyun?
Round-trip tests is bug ko kyun nahi pakad sakte?
Aur kaun se 'two parsers disagree' attacks jaante ho?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Reject vs skip: skip zyada servers ke saath kaam karta, reject parser differential ka risk zero karta. Resolver ke paas next server ka option hai, isliye reject sasta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Bina check ke: misaligned parse se ya WireError baad mein kahin aur (confusing message), ya galat records successfully decode -- sabse bura case.
advanced.alternatives: Har rdata ko apne slice mein parse karna (tab leftover automatically pata chalta, lekin pointers ke liye poora buffer chahiye) ya schema-based parser.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Scale se fark nahi; yeh correctness rule hai. Bade fleet mein lenient parsing se ek bhi buggy upstream poore cache ko corrupt kar sakta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Har record type ke liye 'rdlength +1/-1' mutation ka property test, aur decode errors ko upstream ke naam ke saath metric mein count karna.

question: A mutation that removed the bounds check on a pointer's second byte (W3) left every test green. How was that investigated and fixed?
answer_hinglish:
Symptom: W3 mutation -- 'no bounds check on the second byte of a pointer' -- lagane ke baad poora suite green raha, jabki 'a pointer past the end of the packet is rejected' test mein half pointer ka case already tha. Matlab test tha, lekin woh is check ko test nahi kar raha tha.

Investigation: test kya assert karta hai dekho. Woh sirf expectWireError(withHeader([0xc0])) karta tha -- koi bhi WireError chalega. Mutation ke saath readName ne buf[pos + 1] ko undefined padha, jo bitwise ops mein 0 ban gaya, pointer offset 0 ki taraf gaya (0 < runStart 12, toh 'backwards' rule pass). Offset 0 par header ka pehla byte 0 tha, jo root (zero length) padha gaya, aur naam '' end 14 ke saath 'decode' ho gaya -- jabki buffer sirf 13 bytes ka hai. Phir question ke type field ke liye Reader.need ne WireError phenk diya. Yaani error sahi type ka tha lekin GALAT check se aaya. README ke shabdon mein: 'the half a pointer tests still threw a WireError, but from a LATER check (the question's type field), so the pointer guard itself was untested.'

Cause: test boundary bahut upar (decodeMessage) aur assertion bahut loose (koi bhi WireError).

Fix: naya test 'half a pointer as the very last byte is rejected by readName itself (added after mutation W3)' -- readName ko seedha Buffer.from([0, 0xc0]) par offset 1 se call karta hai aur specific message /truncated: compression pointer/ expect karta hai. Bina check ke wahan pointer offset 0 (ek root byte) par jaata aur naam 'decode' ho jaata ek end offset ke saath jo buffer ke bahar hai. Re-run par W3 exactly is naye test se pakda gaya.
why_needed: Green suite ka matlab yeh nahi ki har guard tested hai. Mutation testing aur specific assertions se pata chalta hai kaunsa code sach mein protected hai.
real_world_analogy: Fire alarm test: aapne dhuaan kiya aur alarm baja -- lekin woh kitchen ka alarm tha, jis room ka test kar rahe the uska alarm toh kharab hai.
how_it_works: Mutation -> suite run -> 0 failures -> test ke error path trace karo (kaun si line throw kar rahi hai) -> unit-level test + specific message regex.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts readName ki line 'if (pos + 1 >= buf.length) throw ... truncated: compression pointer'. test/wire.test.ts W3 test. README mutation table aur 'What was done about the 5' section.
advantages: Specific error message assert karne se test sahi guard ko pin karta hai
Unit-level call (readName) se doosre checks beech mein nahi aate
disadvantages: Error message par assert karne se test message text se coupled ho jaata hai
Mutation checks manual the (ek exact text replacement per check), automated tool nahi
common_mistakes: toThrow(WireError) ko kaafi maan lena
Sirf top-level API se test karna
Mutation 'survived' ko ignore karna
follow_up_questions: Is tarah ke gaps automatically kaise dhoondhoge (Stryker jaisa tool)?
Message regex ke bajaye error code ya subclass better hota?
Undefined ka 0 ban jaana JS mein kahan aur khatarnak hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Precise assertions test ko brittle banate hain (message badla toh test toota), lekin loose assertions guards ko untested chhod dete hain. Yahan precision chuna kyunki yeh security guard hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Bina is guard ke: ek valid-looking naam jiska end buffer ke bahar -- aage ka parser garbage ya alag error se fail. Aur kisi aur code path mein (jaise readName direct use) bug silently pass.
advanced.alternatives: Error codes (WireError ke andar code: 'TRUNCATED_POINTER') par assert, ya har guard ke liye alag subclass. Ya coverage-guided mutation tool (Stryker) jo automatically survived mutants report kare.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Codebase badhega toh manual mutation scale nahi karega; tool-based mutation testing CI mein (nightly) chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Stryker jaisa mutation tool, error codes, aur har bounds check ke liye ek 'exactly this guard' unit test ka convention.

question: A round-trip test fails because a name written as WWW.EXAMPLE.TEST comes back as www.example.test. Is that a bug?
answer_hinglish:
Nahi, yeh design hai, lekin pehli baar dekh ke bug lagta hai. Symptom: encode -> decode ke baad toEqual fail, diff mein answers[3].name 'WWW.EXAMPLE.TEST' expected tha, 'www.example.test' mila.

Investigate kaise: packet ke bytes dekho. Test khud yahi karta hai: small.includes(Buffer.from([0xc0, 12])) -- offset 12 par question name 'www.example.test' hai, aur upper-case repeat ki jagah sirf 2-byte pointer likha gaya. Decoder pointer follow karke offset 12 ke bytes padhta hai -- jo lowercase hain. Original case wire par likha hi nahi gaya.

Cause: Writer.name compression key asciiLower se banata hai. DNS names case-insensitive hain (RFC 4343), toh 'WWW.EXAMPLE.TEST' aur 'www.example.test' same naam hain aur ek doosre ka pointer ban sakte hain. Isse compression zyada hoti hai.

Fix kya hai: code nahi, test aur documentation. Test 'encoding compresses repeated suffixes, case-insensitively, and is much smaller' comparison se pehle expected ko adjust karta hai: fromBig.answers[3].name = 'www.example.test', comment ke saath 'the repeat comes back in the case of the FIRST occurrence'. README mein 'One honest detail' paragraph yahi explain karta hai. Agar kabhi case preserve karna zaroori ho (jaise 0x20 randomisation, jo implement nahi hai), toh compression key case-sensitive karni padegi aur compare mein case check.
why_needed: Behaviour jo bug jaisa dikhe lekin spec ke andar ho, use test aur docs mein likhna padta hai, warna koi baad mein 'fix' karke compression tod dega.
real_world_analogy: Phone book mein 'SHARMA' aur 'Sharma' ek hi entry -- dobara print nahi kiya, toh doosri jagah bhi 'Sharma' hi dikhega.
how_it_works: Writer.name key = asciiLower(escapeLabel(label)) join. Pointer offset pehli occurrence ka. readName target bytes padhta hai, jo pehli occurrence ke case mein hain.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts Writer.name, asciiLower, canonicalName. test/wire.test.ts compression test; README 'One honest detail'; PLAN.md 'a repeated name comes back in the case of its first occurrence (written down, tested)'.

Behaviour documented aur tested, surprise nahi

Cache key mein case kaise handle hota hai?

question: Mutation W4 (no bounds check on a label's bytes) is not caught by any test, yet the check stays. Why is it an equivalent mutant?
answer_hinglish:
Equivalent mutant woh code change hai jo program ke observable behaviour ko badalta hi nahi -- isliye koi behaviour test use kabhi pakad nahi sakta. W4 isi ka example hai.

readName mein label branch: if (pos + 1 + len > buf.length) throw 'truncated: label at offset'. Ise hata do toh kya hota hai? buf.subarray(pos + 1, pos + 1 + len) Node mein out-of-range par chupchaap chhota slice deta hai (crash nahi), toh label cut-short text ban jaata hai. Phir pos += 1 + len -- pos ab buffer ke end se aage. Loop ka agla iteration sabse pehle check karta hai pos >= buf.length -> WireError 'truncated: name at offset X runs past the end'. Yaani same exception type, same moment (us naam ka decode), koi partial result bahar nahi gaya. Cut-short label array mein gaya tha lekin function return hi nahi hua, toh koi observe nahi kar sakta. Sirf error MESSAGE alag hai.

Theoretically message par assert karke test bana sakte ho, lekin README ka conclusion yahi hai: 'cannot be by any behaviour test ... It is an equivalent mutant; the check stays because it gives the right error message.' Aur yeh defence in depth bhi hai: agar kabhi loop ka order badle ya subarray ka behaviour, toh yeh check pehla guard hai.

Interview point: mutation score 100% target nahi hota; survived mutants ko classify karo -- real gap (W3, W7: test jodo) ya equivalent (W4: explain karo, chhod do).
why_needed: Mutation testing ke results ko sahi padhna aana chahiye; har survived mutant test gap nahi hota, aur blindly test likhne se brittle tests bante hain.
real_world_analogy: Ghar mein do taale: andar wala aur bahar wala. Andar wala hata do toh bhi chor bahar wale par hi ruk jaata hai -- test se pata nahi chalega, lekin andar wala taala error message 'yahan ruke' sahi batata hai.
how_it_works: Mutated path: label (no check) -> subarray clamp -> pos > length -> next iteration 'runs past the end' WireError. Original path: label check -> 'truncated: label' WireError. Observable: dono WireError.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts readName label branch aur loop ka first check. README mutation table W4 '0 (not caught)' aur explanation paragraph.
advantages: Sahi error message debugging mein madad karta hai
Defence in depth: doosra guard hatne par bhi safe
disadvantages: Code jo tests se verify nahi hota, uska maintenance trust par hai
Mutation score 100% nahi dikhega
common_mistakes: Har survived mutant ke liye zabardasti test likhna (message-coupled brittle test)
Equivalent mutant ko dead code samajh ke hata dena
Sochna ki subarray out-of-range par throw karta hai
follow_up_questions: W3 bhi survive hua tha -- W3 aur W4 mein kya farak hai?
Equivalent mutants automatically kaise pehchaanoge?
Kya yeh check performance ke liye bhi useful hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Redundant check rakhna thoda code aur ek untestable line deta hai, badle mein accurate error message aur future refactors ke against safety.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar kabhi loop ka first check hata diya jaaye ya loop restructure ho, toh W4 wala check hi out-of-range read rokega; tab mutant equivalent nahi rahega aur test pakdega.
advanced.alternatives: Check hata ke loop guard par bharosa (kam code), ya message-specific test likh ke mutant 'kill' karna (brittle), ya WireError mein error code jo test kar sako.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bade codebase mein equivalent mutants ki list grow hoti hai; mutation tools mein unhe 'ignored' mark karne ka mechanism chahiye taaki har run mein noise na ho.
advanced.production_improvements: Mutation results ka ek file (accepted equivalent mutants with reason) maintain karna, aur automated mutation tool jo us list ko respect kare.

question: How were the wire-format mutation checks W1-W9 run, and what did they reveal about the test suite?
answer_hinglish:
Method simple aur honest tha: har rule ko jaan-boojh ke todo (src/ mein ek exact text replacement), poora suite chalao, file restore karo (git status clean). Check tab 'pass' hota hai jab kam se kam ek test red ho. Pehla run 85 tests ke suite par (76 run + 9 opt-in skipped).

Wire wale nau: W1 pointer forward allowed -> 2 tests fail. W2 no pointer cap -> 1. W3 pointer ke second byte ka bounds check nahi -> 0 (not caught). W4 label bytes ka bounds check nahi -> 0. W5 no 255-byte limit on decoded names -> 1. W6 A record rdlength check nahi -> 1. W7 rdata fewer/more bytes than rdlength -> 0. W8 encoder never compresses -> 2 (aur tsc bhi fail hua unused variable se). W9 Reader.need removed -> 2.

Teen survived. Unka analysis alag-alag nikla. W3: test tha lekin error ek LATER check se aa raha tha -- fix: readName ko seedha [0, 0xc0] par call karne wala test. W7: koi test leftover rdata bytes nahi banata tha (encoder aisa packet kabhi nahi banata, toh round trips blind the) -- fix: NS + 2 junk bytes test. W4: equivalent mutant, koi behaviour test nahi pakad sakta, check error message ke liye rehta hai. Re-run (89-test suite) par W3 aur W7 exactly naye test se pakde gaye.

Poore project mein 41 checks, 36 pehle run mein caught. Lesson: line coverage ne yeh nahi dikhaya hota -- W3 ki line execute ho rahi thi; sirf mutation ne bataya ki uska RESULT kisi assertion se nahi juda.
why_needed: Security-critical parser ke liye 'tests pass' kaafi nahi; dikhana padta hai ki har guard ko koi test sach mein pakadta hai.
real_world_analogy: Security audit mein guard ko jaan-boojh ke so jaane ko kehna aur dekhna ki chori pakdi jaati hai ya nahi. Agar nahi, toh CCTV (test) galat jagah laga hai.
how_it_works: For each rule: patch -> npm test -> count failures -> restore -> verify git status clean. Survived -> classify (gap / equivalent) -> new test -> re-run that mutation.

Sirf chune hue rules todey gaye, saare possible mutants nahi

Restore ke baad git status check na karna

question: Why are names represented as plain strings without a trailing dot (root = "") instead of arrays of label buffers?
answer_hinglish:
Recommendation string thi kyunki baaki poora system -- cache keys, resolver ka zone walk, trace output, tests -- strings ke saath natural hai. 'www.example.test' ko Map key bana sakte ho, log mein print kar sakte ho, test mein literal likh sakte ho. Buffer[] ke saath har jagah join/compare helpers chahiye hote.

Trailing dot kyun nahi: ek hi naam ke do text forms ('a.test' aur 'a.test.') bugs paida karte hain. Ek canonical rule: kabhi trailing dot nahi, root = "". nameToLabels input mein trailing dot accept kar leta hai (user friendly), lekin canonicalName use hata deta hai. formatRecord output mein dot wapas lagata hai, dig jaisa dikhne ke liye.

String ki kamzori: label boundaries text mein encode karni padti hain. Isi liye escapes (\. aur \DDD) zaroori hain, aur comparison kabhi plain string ops (endsWith) se nahi, hamesha isSubdomain/sameName se. Doosri cost: har helper (isSubdomain, parentName, labelCount) naam ko phir se parse karta hai -- performance thodi jaati hai, lekin labels chhote hain.

Alternative Buffer[] labels hota: zero ambiguity aur no re-parsing, lekin API clunky aur cache keys ke liye phir bhi serialise karna padta. PLAN.md ka decision: 'Names are strings without the trailing dot, root = "". Label bytes that are not printable ASCII (and "." or "\" inside a label) use presentation escapes.'
why_needed: Representation decision poore codebase ko touch karta hai; galat chunav har layer mein friction ya bugs laata hai.
real_world_analogy: Address ko ek line mein likhna ('Flat 3, Sector 15, Noida') vs form ke alag boxes. Line handy hai, bas comma wale naam ko quote karna padta hai.
how_it_works: Text form -> nameToLabels -> Buffer[] (sirf encode/compare ke waqt). Decode -> escapeLabel -> joined string. Canonical form: lowercase ASCII, no trailing dot.

Ek canonical form, kam confusion
Escapes se ambiguity khatam
disadvantages: Har helper call par re-parse
Developers ko yaad rakhna padta hai ki string ops (endsWith, ===) use na karein

=== se naam compare karna (case aur escapes miss)
split('.') se labels nikalna

question: The decoder is strict (rejects forward pointers, rdlength mismatches, over-long names). How do you weigh that against Postel's 'be liberal in what you accept'?
answer_hinglish:
Mera jawab: untrusted binary input ke liye strict parsing, lekin system level par resilience. Postel ka principle interop ke liye accha tha, lekin security mein usne bahut nuksaan kiya hai -- lenient parsers ke differences se smuggling aur poisoning hote hain, aur 'accept anything' code mein edge cases untested rehte hain.

Is decoder mein strict rules: pointer sirf backwards (RFC sirf 'prior occurrence' kehta hai -- real servers yahi karte hain), 32 jumps max, label <= 63, naam <= 255, reserved label types 0x40/0x80 reject, A = 4 aur AAAA = 16 bytes exactly, rdata exactly rdlength (W7). Lenient sirf wahan jahan RFC khud kehta hai: unknown types RAW rakhna (RFC 3597), aur 'Bytes after the last record are ignored'.

Strictness ki cost system level par absorb hoti hai: resolver ke liye WireError ek timeout jaisa hai -- next server. Ek zone ke paas typically kai nameservers hote hain, toh ek buggy server ka reject hona lookup fail nahi karta. Stub server malformed query ko FORMERR deta hai, crash nahi.

Evidence ki strictness interop nahi todti: nslookup.exe ke captured packets (test/interop.test.ts) parse hote hain, aur live test real root servers ke against 6/6 pass hua, gmail.com MX aur wikipedia CNAME chain ke saath. Lekin honestly: bade production resolvers kuch broken-zone workarounds rakhte hain, jo README ke NOT-implemented list mein hain.
why_needed: Har protocol implementer ko yeh decision lena padta hai; interviewer dekhta hai ki aap security aur compatibility dono soch sakte ho.
real_world_analogy: Airport security strict hai (har bag scan), lekin airport ke paas kai gates aur flights hain -- ek gate band ho toh doosra. Strict check, resilient system.
how_it_works: Strict decode -> WireError -> caller policy (next server / FORMERR / ignore on UDP). Lenient points: RAW types, trailing bytes.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts saare checks; resolver.ts askZone WireError ko next server se handle karta hai. README live test aur interop sections. PLAN.md compression pointer rule decision.
advantages: Parser differential attacks ka surface chhota
Har rule tested aur mutation-verified
Errors jaldi aur precise
disadvantages: Kuch broken real-world servers ke responses reject ho sakte hain
Har strict rule ek possible interop bug hai jise monitor karna padta hai
common_mistakes: Strict parsing ko 'fail the lookup' samajhna -- strict parse + retry policy alag cheezein hain
Lenient banane ke liye checks hata dena bina yeh soche ki kaunsa attack khulta hai
Interop claim karna bina real servers ke against test kiye
follow_up_questions: Trailing bytes ignore karna lenient hai -- isme koi risk hai?
Agar ek popular zone forward pointers bhejne lage toh kya karoge?
Interop regressions ko production mein kaise detect karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Strict: security aur simplicity, cost kuch interop edge cases. Lenient: compatibility, cost parser differentials aur untested paths. Middle ground: strict parse, resilient caller, aur RFC-mandated leniency (RFC 3597).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar ek zone ke saare servers kisi strict rule par fail karein toh woh zone SERVFAIL hoga -- yeh dikhna chahiye (trace/metrics) taaki pata chale bug hamara hai ya unka.
advanced.alternatives: Lenient-with-warnings mode (accept but log), per-rule feature flags, ya do-pass parsing (strict, fail hone par lenient sirf specific known quirks ke liye).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic aur zyada zones par rare quirks dikhne lagte hain; tab per-rule reject counters chahiye taaki pata chale kaunsa rule real traffic tod raha hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Har WireError reason ka metric (per upstream), sampled packet capture for rejects, aur known-quirk allowlist sirf evidence ke baad.

question: What does the decoder do to stay fast on hostile input, and what do the fuzz tests actually prove about performance?
answer_hinglish:
Seedha jawab: decoder ka har kaam packet size se bounded hai, aur fuzz test ek loose time bound check karta hai -- koi benchmark claim nahi.

Bounds kahan se: har field read bytes consume karta hai aur need() se checked hai; counts se array pre-size nahi hota; har naam max 32 pointers aur 255 bytes; recursion nahi, iterative loop. Toh worst case total kaam roughly packet size x 32 per naam hai, infinite ya exponential nahi. Encode side par Writer 512 bytes se shuru hota hai -- jo UDP DNS ka classic size hai, toh zyaadatar messages bina grow ke -- aur zaroorat par buffer double karta hai, toh appends amortised O(1).

Fuzz test 'fuzz: 3000 random packets and 3000 bit-flipped packets either decode or throw WireError, quickly' prng(15) seed se deterministic hai: 3000 random packets (0-600 bytes, har 7th byte ko 30% chance par pointer byte banaya taaki loop paths chalein) aur valid sample() ke 3000 copies 1-4 bit flips ke saath. Assert: total 6000, rejected > 3000, aur poora loop 5000 ms se kam. Yeh 5 second ka bound sirf 'koi pathological slowdown ya hang nahi' prove karta hai -- performance number nahi hai. README bhi kehta hai ki timings claim nahi kiye gaye.

Compression bhi performance hai: test mein compressed message uncompressed se 100+ bytes chhota hai, jisse zyada replies 512 ke andar rehte hain aur TCP fallback (extra round trips) kam lagta hai.
why_needed: Resolver har reply decode karta hai; agar ek crafted packet CPU kha sake toh woh DoS hai. Bounded work guarantee performance se zyada security property hai.
real_world_analogy: Toll booth jahan har gaadi ko max 32 second milte hain -- koi bhi gaadi line ko ghante bhar nahi rok sakti, chahe kitni bhi ajeeb ho.
how_it_works: Work per packet = O(bytes) + O(names x 32). Writer: grow() doubling. Fuzz: deterministic PRNG, time assertion as a hang detector.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts Reader, readName (MAX_POINTER_JUMPS), Writer.grow. test/wire.test.ts prng aur fuzz tests.

Deterministic fuzz, failure reproduce ho sakta hai
Time bound hang ko pakadta hai
disadvantages: 5 s bound bahut loose -- regressions jo 10x slow karein woh bhi pass ho sakti hain
Koi real benchmark nahi (throughput, allocations)
common_mistakes: Fuzz time bound ko performance claim bana dena
Non-deterministic Math.random se fuzz (failure reproduce nahi hota)
Bit-flip fuzz se maan lena ki deep paths cover ho gaye

escapeLabel ki string allocation hot path mein kitni costly hogi?
Coverage-guided fuzzing random fuzzing se better kyun hai?

question: Why is the wire format a single pure module (src/wire.ts) with one error type, and how do the other layers depend on it?
answer_hinglish:
wire.ts system ka trust boundary hai: internet ke har byte ko sabse pehle yahi chhoota hai, aur har outgoing byte yahi banata hai. Isliye maine use pure aur dependency-free rakha -- sirf node:net ke isIPv4/isIPv6, koi socket nahi, koi clock nahi, koi global state nahi. Input Buffer, output typed Message (ya ulta).

Iske teen fayde. Pehla, testability: wire.test.ts bina kisi network ke har edge case chala sakta hai -- RFC example, loops, truncation at every offset, 6000 fuzz packets. Doosra, ek contract: malformed input par sirf WireError. Upar wali layers ko parsing ki details nahi pata, sirf policy: transport UDP par undecodable ko ignore karta hai, resolver WireError ko next server se handle karta hai, server FORMERR deta hai. Teesra, reuse: wahi encodeMessage resolver ki query, stub server ka reply, aur fake test network ke authoritative replies -- teeno banata hai; aur helpers (canonicalName, isSubdomain, parentName) cache keys aur bailiwick logic ka base hain.

Layering (README diagram): server.ts -> resolver.ts + cache.ts -> transport.ts -> wire.ts. Dependency hamesha neeche ki taraf; wire.ts kisi ko import nahi karta.

Trade-off: name helpers bhi wire.ts mein hain (canonicalName, isSubdomain) jo strictly 'wire' nahi hain. Maine unhe yahan rakha kyunki woh nameToLabels aur escapeLabel par tike hain -- escaping ka ek hi source of truth. Bade codebase mein main names.ts alag karta.
why_needed: Untrusted input ko ek chhote, pure, heavily tested module mein band karna security aur maintainability ka standard pattern hai.
real_world_analogy: Factory ka quality-check gate: bahar se aane wala har raw material wahin check hota hai, andar ki machines maan sakti hain ki unhe jo mila woh valid hai.
how_it_works: Bytes -> decodeMessage -> Message (typed) -> resolver/cache/server. Message -> encodeMessage -> Bytes. Errors -> WireError -> caller policy.

Importers: transport.ts, resolver.ts, server.ts, cache.ts. README Files table: 'message types, encode/decode, name compression, name helpers'.

Ek codec teen jagah reuse (client, server, fake network)

Typed Message banane mein allocations; zero-copy views nahi

question: If you treat the cache as a data store, what is the key format for names, and why must canonicalization happen in wire.ts rather than in the cache?
answer_hinglish:
Cache ek key-value store hai jismein positive RRsets ka key '<canonical name>|<type>' aur NXDOMAIN ka key '<canonical name>|NX' hai (src/cache.ts mein posKey aur nxKey). Key ka naam hissa canonicalName() se aata hai, jo wire.ts mein hai: ASCII lowercase, no trailing dot, escapes ke saath. Toh 'WWW.Example.TEST.' aur 'www.example.test' ek hi row hain.

Yeh normalisation codec ke paas kyun: key ki correctness naam ke text form par depend karti hai, aur text form ka source of truth wire.ts hai -- escapeLabel decide karta hai ki label ka dot '\.' banega aur non-printable byte '\DDD'. Agar cache apna lowercase() karta (JS ka toLowerCase), toh do problems: woh non-ASCII ya escaped bytes ke saath alag behave kar sakta hai, aur ek label 'a.b' aur do labels 'a' + 'b' ek hi key ban sakte the. canonicalName sirf A-Z ko lowercase karta hai (asciiLower) -- 'Case of other bytes is kept', jaisa DNS rules (RFC 4343) kehte hain.

Database terms mein: canonicalName ek normalisation function hai jaise email ko lowercase karke unique index banana -- normalisation hamesha ek jagah, write aur read dono par same. Record ka data model bhi wire.ts deta hai: ResourceRecord { name, type, class, ttl, data: RData } aur TTL hi expiry column hai. Cache ka TTL math aur ranking is file ka topic nahi hai -- yahan point key normalisation ka hai.
why_needed: Key normalisation galat ho toh duplicates (same naam do baar cache) ya collisions (do alag naam ek key) -- dono cache bugs aur collision ho toh poisoning jaisa effect.
real_world_analogy: Library catalogue mein 'Premchand', 'PREMCHAND', 'premchand.' sab ek hi card -- lekin 'Prem Chand' (alag author) alag card. Normalisation rule ek hi librarian ke paas.
how_it_works: canonicalName = nameToLabels(name).map(l => asciiLower(escapeLabel(l))).join('.'). cache.ts: posKey(name, type) = canonicalName(name) + '|' + type.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts canonicalName, asciiLower, ResourceRecord; src/cache.ts posKey aur nxKey canonicalName use karte hain. Test 'canonicalName lowercases ASCII and drops the trailing dot'.

Escapes ki wajah se collisions impossible

disadvantages: Har cache access par naam parse hota hai
Composite key string concatenation se -- separator '|' par bharosa (naam mein '|' printable hai, lekin type numeric hai toh last '|' unambiguous)
