question: Many lookups run concurrently in one Node process. Why is the codec safe to share, and what part of the wire format lets concurrent queries be told apart?
answer_hinglish:
Codec safe hai kyunki usme koi shared mutable state nahi hai. decodeMessage har call par naya Reader banata hai (apna pos), aur encodeMessage har message ke liye naya Writer -- uska compression map (names) aur buffer sirf us ek message ke hain. Module level par sirf constants hain (TYPE, RCODE, TYPE_NAMES). Node single-threaded hai toh data race waise bhi nahi, lekin async interleaving mein bhi koi bug nahi aa sakta kyunki encode/decode synchronous hain aur beech mein await nahi -- ek message ka encode doosre ke beech mein ghus hi nahi sakta. Agar Writer ka map module-level hota, toh ek message ke offsets doosre message mein pointer ban jaate -- corrupted packets.

Concurrent queries ko alag karne ka wire-level tool header ka 16-bit ID hai, plus question section jo response mein echo hota hai. Wire.ts ID ko bas encode/decode karta hai; matching transport.ts mein hai (random ID, random port, exact question match) -- woh doosre file ka topic hai. Lekin format level par samjho: 16 bits ka matlab 65536 values, isliye sirf ID par bharosa spoofing ke liye kamzor hai.

Distributed angle: wire format hi woh contract hai jo alag implementations (nslookup.exe, real root servers, hamara resolver) ko jodta hai. TCP par message ke aage 2-byte length aata hai (64 KB max) -- isi liye encodeMessage 65535 se bade message ko reject karta hai.
why_needed: Shared mutable state concurrency bugs ka sabse common source hai; codec ko stateless rakhna async server mein correctness ki guarantee hai.
real_world_analogy: Har courier ke paas apni notebook (Writer) -- agar sab ek hi notebook mein 'yeh address page 12 par hai' likhein toh sabke parcels mein galat references.
how_it_works: Per-call Reader/Writer -> no shared state. Header ID + echoed question -> reply matching (transport layer). TCP: 2-byte length prefix -> message <= 65535.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts: Reader aur Writer per call, encodeMessage ka 'message longer than 65535 bytes' check, buildQuery(id, ...). ID generation aur matching src/transport.ts mein.
advantages: Stateless codec: koi lock, koi race nahi
Worker threads mein bhi bina change ke chal sakta hai
Har message apne aap mein complete
disadvantages: Har message naya Writer aur 512-byte buffer allocate karta hai (koi pooling nahi)
16-bit ID khud mein spoofing ke liye kaafi nahi
common_mistakes: Writer/compression map ko performance ke liye reuse karna bina reset ke
Sochna ki ID unique hona hi concurrency ke liye kaafi hai
Encode mein await daal dena (tab interleaving ka risk)
follow_up_questions: In-flight deduplication (implement nahi hai) kaise karoge?
Worker threads mein decode le jaana kab worth hai?
Writer pooling karoge toh kya reset karna zaroori hoga?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Stateless per-call objects simplicity aur safety dete hain; cost har message ki allocation. Pooling se GC kam hoga lekin reset bugs (stale compression map) ka risk.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar compression map share ho jaata toh doosre message ke offsets ke pointers -- decoder pe forward/garbage pointers, ya worse, valid lekin galat naam.
advanced.alternatives: Buffer pool with explicit reset, ya worker_threads mein decoding (CPU parallelism) -- Node mein decode bahut chhota kaam hai, toh thread hop ka overhead zyada ho sakta hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x QPS par event loop CPU-bound ho sakta hai; tab cluster mode (multiple processes) codec ke stateless hone ki wajah se seedha kaam karega. Measure nahi kiya.
advanced.production_improvements: Allocation profiling, optional Writer pool, aur in-flight dedupe (README mein NOT implemented) taaki identical concurrent queries ek hi upstream packet banayein.

question: A real upstream reply contains an OPT record, RRSIG records and is close to 512 bytes. How does this codec handle it today, and what would production need?
answer_hinglish:
Aaj: decode safe hai, lekin features nahi hain. OPT (type 41) aur RRSIG/DS jaise DNSSEC types TYPE map mein (OPT hai, RRSIG nahi) structured parse nahi hote -- readRData ke default case mein RAW ban jaate hain, bytes waise hi. OPT record ka 'class' field asal mein UDP payload size hai aur TTL field extended rcode/flags; hum use ordinary record ki tarah padhte hain aur ignore karte hain. Toh reply crash nahi karta, records cache tak RAW pahunch sakte hain, lekin koi validation nahi. Is project mein DNSSEC aur EDNS(0) implement nahi hain -- README ke NOT-implemented list mein pehle do items.

512 bytes: hum kabhi OPT nahi bhejte, toh upstream classic rule follow karta hai -- UDP reply 512 bytes tak, zyada ho toh TC=1, aur resolver TCP par dobara poochta hai (resolver/transport ka kaam). Stub server bhi client ka OPT ignore karta hai aur UDP 512 par cap karta hai.

Production ko kya chahiye: (1) EDNS(0) encode -- har query mein additional section mein OPT with payload size (typically 1232 aaj ka common choice), taaki kam TCP fallbacks; (2) OPT decode as structured data (payload size, DO bit, extended rcode, options); (3) DNSSEC: RRSIG, DNSKEY, DS, NSEC/NSEC3 parse + canonical wire form (RFC 4034 -- lowercase names, NO compression) for signature verification -- yahan hamara canonicalName aur compress: false wala path kaam aa sakta hai; (4) encoder mein message size budget taaki responses truncate sahi tareeke se hon.
why_needed: Real internet par lagbhag har modern response mein OPT hota hai aur signed zones RRSIG bhejte hain. Interviewer dekhta hai ki aap project ki seemayein jaante ho aur next step bata sakte ho.
real_world_analogy: Ek purana translator jo naye shabd (OPT, RRSIG) ko samajh nahi paata, lekin unhe chhodta bhi nahi -- jaise ke waise copy karke aage de deta hai. Kaam chalta hai, lekin unka matlab use nahi pata.
how_it_works: Unknown/OPT -> RAW (RFC 3597). No OPT sent -> 512 limit -> TC -> TCP. DNSSEC: not implemented.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts TYPE (OPT: 41), RData RAW ('Any type we do not understand (and OPT)'), readRData default, formatRecord '\#' form. README 'NOT implemented yet': DNSSEC validation, EDNS(0). PLAN.md 'Not in scope'.
advantages: Unknown types se kabhi crash nahi
TCP fallback se bade answers bhi milte hain
Roadmap clear: codec mein jagah hai (RAW -> structured)
disadvantages: Har bada answer extra TCP round trip leta hai
DNSSEC ke bina spoofing ka asli ilaaj nahi
OPT ka extended rcode ignore -- kuch errors galat dikhenge
common_mistakes: Sochna ki RAW decode = support
OPT ko normal record ki tarah cache kar lena
DNSSEC ke liye compressed names par signature verify karna (canonical form uncompressed lowercase hai)
follow_up_questions: EDNS payload size kitna rakhoge aur kyun (fragmentation)?
DNSSEC validation chain root se kaise chalti hai?
OPT record ko cache se kaise bahar rakhoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Abhi simplicity: no OPT, 512 + TCP. EDNS se kam round trips lekin fragmentation risk aur zyada code. DNSSEC security deta hai lekin crypto, key management aur bahut complexity.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Bade UDP payloads (EDNS bina sensible limit ke) IP fragmentation laate hain jo firewalls drop karte hain -- timeouts. DNSSEC galat implement ho toh valid zones bogus (SERVFAIL).
advanced.alternatives: EDNS ke bajaye hamesha TCP (simple lekin slow), DoT/DoH upstream (transport security, lekin authenticity nahi), ya DNSSEC-validating library use karna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100x traffic par TCP fallbacks connection overhead badhate hain; EDNS(0) yahan pehla improvement hoga. DNSSEC validation CPU cost add karta hai (signature verify) -- caching of validated results zaroori.
advanced.production_improvements: OPT encode/decode stage, payload size config, structured RRSIG/DNSKEY/DS types, canonical wire form function, aur validation ke liye alag module.

question: Add support for SRV records (type 33: priority, weight, port, target) to the codec, with a round-trip test.
answer_hinglish:
SRV ka rdata RFC 2782 mein hai: priority (u16), weight (u16), port (u16), aur target naam. Kaam chaar jagah: TYPE map mein SRV: 33, RData union mein naya variant, readRData mein case, writeRData aur writeRDataNoCompress mein case, aur formatRecord mein text.

Ek important RFC point: SRV ka target naam compress NAHI hona chahiye. RFC 3597 kehta hai ki sirf purane well-known types (RFC 1035 wale: NS, CNAME, SOA, MX, PTR...) ke rdata mein compression allowed hai; SRV baad ka type hai. Decode par compressed target accept karna theek hai (kuch servers bhejte hain, tolerant decode), lekin encode par hum w.name(target, false) likhenge.

readRData mein: rdlength kam se kam 7 (6 bytes numbers + 1 byte root naam), teen u16, phir name() closure -- jo check karta hai ki naam rdlength ke andar hai -- aur function ke end ka existing r.pos !== rdEnd check apne aap leftover bytes pakad lega. Isliye har naye type ko bas inhi helpers ke through padhna chahiye.

Test: ek message banao jisme _sip._tcp.example.test SRV 10 60 5060 sip.example.test ho, encode -> decode toEqual, aur ek negative case: rdlength 6 -> WireError. Wire.test.ts ke rr() aur buildQuery helpers reuse karo. Note: yeh exercise hai, repo mein SRV abhi RAW decode hota hai.
why_needed: Naya record type jodna codec ki structure samajhne ka best test hai: union, decode, encode, limits, compression rules sab ek saath.
real_world_analogy: Ek form mein naya section jodna: form template (union), bharne ka tareeka (encode), padhne ka tareeka (decode), aur validation (rdlength).
how_it_works: TYPE.SRV = 33 -> decode case (3 x u16 + name) -> encode case (3 x u16 + uncompressed name) -> format -> tests (round trip + short rdlength).
in_this_project: src/wire.ts ke readRData, writeRData, writeRDataNoCompress, formatRecord, TYPE, RData mein changes; test/wire.test.ts mein rr() helper aur buildQuery. Abhi SRV default case mein RAW hai.
advantages: Existing helpers (name closure, final rdlength check) se naya type safe
Union ki wajah se TypeScript har switch mein missing case batayega (formatRecord, writeRData)
disadvantages: Har naye type ke liye chaar jagah edit -- table-driven schema se kam hota
Uncompressed target thoda bada packet
common_mistakes: SRV target ko compress karna
name() closure ke bajaye r.name() seedha use karna (rdlength guard skip)
writeRDataNoCompress mein case bhoolna
follow_up_questions: Decode par compressed SRV target accept karna sahi hai ya nahi?
Resolver SRV ke additional section ke A records ko bailiwick ke hisaab se kaise treat karega?
